```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(janitor)
```
```{r}
SchoolData <- read_csv(
  "science_all_students_2018_19.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)

names(SchoolData)
```
```{r}
SchoolData <- clean_names(SchoolData)
names(SchoolData)
```
```{r}
SchoolData %>% distinct(test_subject)

SchoolData %>% distinct(organization_level)

SchoolData %>% distinct(student_group_type, student_group)

SchoolData %>% distinct(grade_level)

SchoolData %>% distinct(test_administration)
```
```{r}
ScienceData <- SchoolData %>%
  filter(
    test_subject == "Science",
    student_group == "All Students",
    grade_level == "All Grades"
  )

ScienceData %>%
  distinct(organization_level, test_administration)
```
```{r}
ScienceSchools <- ScienceData %>%
  filter(organization_level == "School")

ScienceSchools %>%
  dplyr::select(
    county,
    school_name,
    test_administration,
    suppression,
    count_of_students_expected_to_test,
    count_met_standard
  ) %>%
  head()
```
```{r}
ScienceSchools <- ScienceSchools %>%
  mutate(
    count_of_students_expected_to_test =
      parse_number(count_of_students_expected_to_test, na = "NULL"),
    count_met_standard =
      parse_number(count_met_standard, na = "NULL")
  )

ScienceSchools %>%
  dplyr::select(
    count_of_students_expected_to_test,
    count_met_standard
  ) %>%
  head()
```
```{r}
CountyScience <- ScienceSchools %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(count_of_students_expected_to_test),
    !is.na(count_met_standard),
    count_of_students_expected_to_test > 0
  ) %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  summarise(
    expected = sum(count_of_students_expected_to_test),
    met = sum(count_met_standard)
  ) %>%
  mutate(percent_met = met / expected * 100)

CountyScience
```
```{r}
StateScience <- ScienceData %>%
  filter(organization_level == "State") %>%
  mutate(
    count_of_students_expected_to_test =
      parse_number(count_of_students_expected_to_test, na = "NULL"),
    count_met_standard =
      parse_number(count_met_standard, na = "NULL")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    test_administration,
    count_of_students_expected_to_test,
    count_met_standard
  )

StateScience
```
```{r}
StateAverage <- StateScience %>%
  summarise(
    expected = sum(count_of_students_expected_to_test),
    met = sum(count_met_standard)
  ) %>%
  mutate(state_percent = met / expected * 100)

StateAverage
```
```{r}
CountyScience <- CountyScience %>%
  mutate(
    state_diff = percent_met - StateAverage$state_percent,
    state_compare = case_when(
      state_diff > 0 ~ "Above state average",
      state_diff < 0 ~ "Below state average",
      state_diff == 0 ~ "Equal to state average"
    )
  )

CountyScience %>%
  group_by(state_compare) %>%
  summarise(counties = n())
```
```{r}
WashingtonMap <- st_read(
  "Week 2 Homework boundaries-20261105/Washington_Counties_with_Natural_Shoreline___washsh_area.shp"
)

WashingtonMap <- clean_names(WashingtonMap)

names(WashingtonMap)
```
```{r}
WashingtonScienceMap <- WashingtonMap %>%
  left_join(CountyScience, by = "county")

WashingtonScienceMap %>%
  filter(is.na(percent_met)) %>%
  dplyr::select(county)
```
```{r}
WashingtonScienceMap <- WashingtonMap %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county)) %>%
  left_join(CountyScience, by = "county")

WashingtonScienceMap %>%
  filter(is.na(percent_met)) %>%
  dplyr::select(county)
```
```{r}
library(tmap)
tmap_mode("plot")

tm_shape(WashingtonScienceMap) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "state_compare",
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Compared with state average")
  ) +
  tm_title("Science attainment, Washington, 2018–19")
```

Data: The included CSV is a subset of Report_Card_Assessment_Data_2018-19_School_Year_20241008.csv, downloaded from the course materials. Column names were cleaned using clean_names(), and records were retained where test_subject = "Science", student_group = "All Students", and grade_level = "All Grades". All other columns and organization levels were retained. County boundaries are supplied in the accompanying “Week 2 Homework boundaries-20261105” folder.
To reproduce: Install tidyverse, sf, janitor and tmap (version 4 or later), keep the supplied files together, and Knit washington_science.Rmd to HTML.
